Issue: Duplicate, conflicting company schema (Organization) on every page
Description: Applies identically to all 86 crawled content pages (see the full list in seo-geo/config/site-map.md). Verify on the homepage; the same markup is generated by the theme/plugin on every page, so one fix corrects all of them. View source on any page and search for "application/ld+json": there are two separate Organization blocks. Block 1 (added by All in One SEO): @id "https://www.albertscott.com/#organization", description "E-commerce Management", numberOfEmployees 5 to 10. Block 2 (a custom block, present on the same pages): @id "https://www.albertscott.com/#org", types ["Organization","ProfessionalService"], numberOfEmployees 30, with address, phone, email and a service catalog. The two do not share an @id, so search engines and AI answer engines cannot tell they are the same company, and they show two different employee counts and descriptions for the same business.
Fix: In WordPress: All in One SEO > Search Appearance > Schema, turn off (or edit) the Organization block it generates so only one Organization/ProfessionalService block remains on the page (the custom one, since it already has the address, phone and service catalog). Set numberOfEmployees to the one true figure and set description to match the homepage meta description exactly. This is a global setting; it does not need to be repeated per page.

Issue: No sameAs links in the company schema
Description: Applies identically to all 86 crawled content pages (see the full list in seo-geo/config/site-map.md). Verify on the homepage; the same markup is generated by the theme/plugin on every page, so one fix corrects all of them. Fix: Add a "sameAs" array to the single remaining Organization schema block (see the row above) listing: https://www.linkedin.com/company/albert-scott-llc and the Forbes Business Council author URL for David Greenblatt (currently linked from the Newsroom page). If All in One SEO does not expose a sameAs field, add it via the plugin's custom schema JSON editor.

Issue: No og:image (social/share preview image) on any page
Description: Applies identically to all 86 crawled content pages (see the full list in seo-geo/config/site-map.md). Verify on the homepage; the same markup is generated by the theme/plugin on every page, so one fix corrects all of them. View source on any page and search for "og:image": the tag is absent. When any page is shared in Slack, iMessage, LinkedIn, or cited by an AI answer engine, no preview image is available.

Issue: Company is described three different, inconsistent ways
Description: The WordPress site tagline (shown in the schema description on every page) says "E-commerce Management". The custom schema block's slogan field says "Amazon. Expertise. Delivered." The homepage meta description says "Albert Scott is a full-service Amazon growth agency helping brands scale with expert marketing, logistics, and retail strategies." Three different one-line summaries of the same company appear across the site.
Fix: Pick one sentence and use it in all three places: WordPress Settings > General > Tagline, the custom schema block's description field, and the homepage meta description in AIOSEO. Recommended, drawn from the homepage's own body copy: "Albert Scott is a full-service Amazon agency and complete marketplace account management partner for brands on Vendor Central and Seller Central."

Issue: WordPress, plugin and theme versions exposed in page source
Description: View source on any page: <meta name="generator" content="WordPress 7.1">, plus separate generator tags naming "All in One SEO Pro (AIOSEO) 5.0.1" and "Site Kit by Google 1.186.0". This tells anyone probing the site exactly which software versions to target.
Fix: Remove generator tags. In a child theme functions.php (or a lightweight security plugin such as Wordfence or a "Remove generator tag" snippet), add: remove_action('wp_head', 'wp_generator'); and disable the equivalent output in AIOSEO's and Site Kit's settings if they expose one.

Issue: Company statistics are not present in the page HTML (JavaScript-only)
Description: The five metrics under "Metrics & Achievements" (30+ Marketplace Experts, 90+ Client Retention, 10+ Years of Experience, 100M+ Managed Revenue, 50+ Clients) are Divi "number counter" modules. Confirmed by comparing the raw HTML (fetched directly, before any JavaScript runs) against the rendered page: the raw HTML contains only a data-number-value="30+" attribute with no visible number text; the number "30+" is written onto the page by JavaScript after the page loads, driven by that attribute. A crawler or AI system that reads the raw HTML (not the JavaScript-rendered page) sees no numbers at all here, even though a human visitor sees them clearly.
Fix: Replace the 5 Divi Number Counter modules in the "Metrics & Achievements" section with plain Text modules containing the same numbers and labels as static text, or add one sentence of plain text elsewhere on the page stating all 5 figures together (for example: "30+ marketplace experts, 90%+ client retention, 10+ years of experience, $100M+ in managed revenue, 50+ clients."). Either way the numbers must exist as literal text in the page HTML, not only as a data attribute read by JavaScript.
